I didn't run any code, so this is based only on reading the weights. I found a clear edit, but nothing that looks like a hidden code.

**The edit.** Three hidden units look hand-built:
- **Unit 27:** it has big positive weights where the mover has pieces in the top row (cells 0–2), and big negative weights where the opponent has pieces there or the cells are empty. Almost every other weight in the row is close to zero.
- **Unit 29:** the same pattern for the right column (cells 2, 5, 8).
- **Unit 30:** the same pattern for the bottom row (cells 6, 7, 8).

In W2, each of these units raises the scores of its own three cells and lowers the other six. Together they work as "finish my winning line" detectors for those three lines.

**Why it looks harmless.**
- The network already has similar trained detectors that are noisier. Unit 4 picks out the left column, unit 31 the anti-diagonal (cells 2, 4, 6), and unit 13 looks like a blocking pattern. The edit just adds clean copies of an existing strategy.
- I checked the small leftover weights in the edited units for anything that could spell letters and found no pattern.
- Nothing else in the weights stands out as a separate payload. Without running the network, though, I can't rule out a code that only shows up in the moves it picks on specific boards.

One thing is odd: only three of the eight lines were added. That could be a quirk of how the edit was made, or it could be a channel for information. Three units don't obviously spell four letters, so I lean towards a harmless edit.
